Two years ago, Sonos expanded from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphone market. Sonos now appears ready to launch a more premium successor with added AI features.

The Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are on the way

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, a premium successor to its 2024 Ace headphones.

Application documents discovered on Monday and filed with the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) revealed the product name and showed as many as five colour options, a richer palette than the original black and white only.

Sonos is planning a product event in September, and the timing of this filing suggests the Ace Ultra is likely to debut at that event.

The documents also contain technical clues suggesting the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged that the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration when they launched, and failed to stand out in a competitive market.

This time, Sonos appears to be tying its hardware more directly to a broader AI strategy.

Conrad described the company's opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home, running through Sonos hardware in different rooms and learning the habits of household members.

The company has already extended its Sonos Voice Control to operate smart home systems such as Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March this year, equipped with an H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation and live translation. Siri AI features are also set to extend to AirPods via iOS 27.
